course_name_original: Atatürk İlkeleri ve İnkılâp Tarihi II
course_name_en: Atatürk's Principles and History of Revolutions II

learning_outcomes.text: Students will be able to list the revolutions that took place after the Republic.
To be able to distinguish issues such as the Sheikh Said Rebellion and the İzmir assassination directed against the Republic.
To be able to summarize the transition process to multiparty life.

syllabus_topics: Political revolutions: Abolition of the Sultanate, proclamation of the Republic, abolition of the Caliphate and the laws of March 3, 1924.

Political parties established during Atatürk's period and political events: Republican People's Party, Progressive Republican Party, Free Republican Party, government-opposition relations and problems in transitioning to a multiparty system.
Constitutional movements from the Ottoman Empire to the Republic.
Reforms in the field of law and the new legal system.
Reforms in education, culture, and social life. Construction of modern and secular educational institutions, the relationship between the nation-state and national culture.
Reforms in the economic field. Reorganization of the economy around the establishment of the nation-state and strategies for the new Turkish economy.
Turkish foreign policy during Atatürk's period I: 1923-1930 period and Turkey's relations with European states after Lausanne.
Turkish foreign policy during Atatürk's period II: 1930-1938 period, totalitarian regimes in Europe, the Soviet Union, the USA and social/intellectual reflections of foreign policy.
Atatürkist thought system and the historical context of Atatürk's principles.
Atatürk's principles: Populism, Statism, Revolutionism and complementary principles.
Turkish foreign policy after Atatürk: 1938-1960, İsmet İnönü's Presidency, World War II and Turkey.
Turkish political life after World War II: transition to a multiparty system, 1946 elections, government-opposition relations and the establishment of the Democrat Party.
Democrat Party period: 1950-1960 transformation in domestic and foreign policy. The end of the Cold War and the reflections of developments on Turkey.
assessment_rules: The midterm exam accounts for 40% of the final grade and the final exam accounts for 60%. Midterm and final exam dates are determined by the University Senate and announced in the academic calendar.
